componentScenarios.expect: Initial hydration, refresh and reconnect read exactly one summary page per visible collection; no cursor drain, detail fanout or unconditional full list read.
With more than limit active scripts, show the first page as partial and Load more; one next-page read per explicit action, no automatic refill after local grouping.
With 250 active monitors across 50 owners and limit100, first read shows100 and Load more; separate actions reveal100 then50, and only the final response marks complete.

A first active page of100 oneOff rows may hide older saved rows; retain purpose metadata and collection Load more, show only loaded counts, do not claim saved is empty globally or fetch more automatically.
An empty local agent group on a partial workspace monitor page does not prove that agent has no active monitors; keep workspace Load more available.
Only an explicit user-requested full-data operation such as export may traverse all cursors without individual Load more actions; routine hydration and badge refresh may not.
Full shapes/order survive, but only unarchived scripts/active monitors; archive all/archived and state all/terminal fail -32602 before selection. Protocol14 breaks old history assumptions.
Require protocol14 and exact feature capability; unsupported is explicit, with no archive/history/full-list fallback.
Missing summary discriminator invalidates support; do not accept ignored cursor or loop.
Reject method/workspace/filter mismatch; authorize every page independently.
Unknown and foreign IDs indistinguishable after workspace authorization; MCP monitor detail remains owner-scoped.
Deleting the boundary or an earlier row does not skip surviving rows on the next page.
Live pages deduplicate IDs and reconcile events; omission from a partial page never deletes or reseeds.
Older get reply cannot overwrite newer full script:changed or script:state snapshots.
Delayed active summary cannot revive a settled canonical monitor.
Read only the first active monitor page on initial badge hydration; zero full script-list, get, output or monitorDetails reads for collapsed badges, including on script events.
At most one monitor detail and one referenced script get; no bulk detail hydration.
Complete selected definitions preserve env/cwd; never execute, compare, copy or persist preview text as a command.
Selected archived script uses only known-ID script.output(maxLines) and optional script.status; no get, enumeration, restore or restart.
Active monitor detail remains available until its terminal deletion; afterward get is InvalidParams. Output is not historical run output.
Full script and monitor lifecycle event snapshots survive; monitor terminal mutations return receipts, never stored finished rows.
Summary/list/get do not settle active monitors, renew TTL or change ownership; terminal rows are deleted by lifecycle arbitration.
Assert storage/registry selection excludes archived keys before loading definition bodies in every list view; obsolete filter validation performs no query.
After completed/triggered/expired/cancelled commit, monitor storage/list/get contain no terminal row; notification work survives separately.
Reconnect a selected archived ID with output/status only, preserving its tab and not editing a preview.
start returns run-a; it exits before monitor(runId:run-a); run-finished refuses with run-a and no monitor/wake. Caller handles status/output immediately instead of ending turn to wait.
A successor run-b starts after run-a refusal. Initial status run-b prevents output attribution and prevents blind registration without runId.
Status before output says run-a, status after says run-b. Discard refused-run output attribution; no retry/rearm or archive enumeration.
Missing runId in refusal/status is unsupported for run-specific attribution, not permission to read a different run or wait for a fabricated monitor.
